FITNESS TEST

At a glance

The Norwegian Armed Forces has several fitness tests for different stages and roles. The 3,000 m run is one familiar part, but there is no single time that applies to everyone.

FEATURED ACTIVITY3,000 m runSee the official table for your test

What the test includes

  • 3,000 m run
  • Pull-ups
  • Standing long jump
  • Medicine-ball throw

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

General soldier tests comprise running and three strength/power assessments. Selection-day and annual employee protocols may differ; the applicable role determines the required grade.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

Scoring and scope

These are examples from the general grading table, not a universal pass standard. The horizontal and hanging pull-up variants are not directly interchangeable. Use the current role-specific table.

  • Selection-day fitness test
  • Annual employee fitness test

Before you rehearse the test

  1. Record the exact pull-up variant, the medicine-ball mass and the measuring method for each jump or throw.
  2. For a 3,000 m run on a measured 400 m track, seven and a half laps are required. Work out a sustainable lap split from your target time rather than sprinting the first lap.

Medicine-ball throw

Use the prescribed 10 kg medicine ball. Follow the official starting position and measuring method; the best of three attempts counts. Practise the movement with a manageable load before using test equipment.

Standing long jump

Start with both feet behind the line and jump from two feet. Distance is measured to the rearmost landing point, so a backward step can reduce the result. Practise a balanced landing.

Pull-ups

For hanging repetitions, use an overhand grip and raise the chin above the bar from the prescribed starting position. The horizontal variation supports the heels and is scored separately. Record which variation you perform.

3,000 m run

Use the measured distance and elapsed time. The assessor may instead use the published 20 m shuttle protocol; these are separate tests with separate grading tables.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Alternate easy running with controlled intervals, then use a measured 3,000 m route to calibrate pacing.
  • Develop explosive strength with low-volume jumps and throws, with full recovery between repetitions.
  • Build pulling strength using strict repetitions, controlled lowering and appropriate horizontal variations.

Putting it into a training week

Use a measured route for a controlled baseline. Alternate an easy run with a pacing session, and practise a few fresh, high-quality jumps and throws before strength work.

Common mistakes

  • Using GPS distance alone on a short assessment route or comparing different pull-up variants as identical.
  • Repeated maximal throws and jumps when fatigued; overlooking the specific protocol used at selection.

What to log

Record run time, ball mass, best throw, best jump and pull-up variant plus valid repetition count.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

  • The required result depends on which test is being taken and the relevant official criteria.
  • Check the tables on the Norwegian Armed Forces website rather than relying on a single number.
